analysis.title: Everyone Wants Nuclear Power, Nobody Wants Nuclear Stocks: Inside The Great Uprate Rush
key_insights: Goldman's nuclear coverage averaged -21% over three months vs +3% for the S&P 500. OKLO fell 29%, the weakest in coverage, attributed to risk-off sentiment toward advanced nuclear developers and limited near-term commercial catalysts.
NuScale short interest rose 16% in a month, the largest jump. UEC short interest fell 14%, which Goldman reads as relatively more constructive positioning toward uranium-focused names.

Between Sep 22 and Oct 20 the hyperscalers and Washington signed, funded or floated at least nine US nuclear deals, including Google's 3,590MW deal with Constellation (890MW new capacity from 11 existing reactors), Amazon's 20-year Calvert Cliffs PPA with Constellation, and a DOE loan of about $4 billion to Vistra for uprates.

Scotiabank estimates the Google deal could add as much as $2/sh of EPS (+~10%) for CEG. CEG traded above $300 on Oct 6 and was at $263 two weeks later, down 7.4% in the last week and 26.4% YTD per JPMorgan. JPMorgan's desk saw supply in CEG as investors reduced exposure after contracting wins.

Raymond James says the Amazon and Google agreements largely commit the ~1 GW of uprates in CEG's ~5-GW PJM Cycle 1 pipeline, leaving ~4 GW of gas, storage and other development. Pricing on the new PPAs is undisclosed.

CIBC initiated CEG (PT $358) and TLN (PT $499) and says the market assigns insufficient value to CEG's contracting upside. HSBC rates all four IPPs (CEG, NRG, VST, TLN) Buy in its 28-utility initiation.

The NRC lists ~30 expected uprate applications through 2032 totaling ~2.4GW, led by Constellation (12), Duke (5), Southern (4) and Vistra (4). UBS counts 2,421MW of planned uprates against a 5,000MW target by 2030, 2,255MW of restarts and ~14GW of large new build, mostly with FID TBD.

HSBC says nuclear tax credits (floor of c$45/MWh), PJM capacity payments (c$14-15/MWh uplift), PJM forwards above $60/MWh and long-term PPAs have raised and derisked US nuclear profitability. It models Constellation's implied nuclear price rising from the mid-$40s/MWh in 2022-24 to the mid-$80s by 2029/30, with 75% of the fleet contracted by 2032. The tax credit is guaranteed only through 2032.
BloombergNEF (via Needham) sees 13.7GW of US nuclear additions through 2036 versus up to 67.8GW of new gas through 2030.

X-energy signed a second Amazon-backed project, a ~960MW, 12-SMR plant in Indiana with AEP. The stock is at $10.36, 71% below its high, with a $4.1 billion market cap. Amazon owned ~23% of Class A shares as of June 30. The AMZN PPA depends on a positive FID. JPMorgan wants firm offtake, financing, capex and licensing timeline before confidence returns. UBS says focus stays on the Seadrift project in Texas, with construction approval expected in early 2027.

Deep Fission has a master energy purchase agreement for 150MW in Kansas (COD 3Q28), but the counterparty has no minimum purchase obligation. Cash is ~$72 million at end of 3Q and ~$40 million by year-end, burn is ~$3 million a month, and about $90 million is still to be spent on the pilot. Canaccord expects the company to need additional capital.

Needham's nuclear reactor basket fell 19.2% in the week to Oct 16, down 50.6% over six months and 74.6% over twelve. The fuel-cycle basket is down 76.3% over a year. Needham attributes the weakness to repricing of financing and execution risk, with data center capex underwritten above $13MM/MW and dilutive converts such as CIFR's $850 million.
OKLO at $27.97 is 84% below its 52-week high, NNE 74% below, LEU 72% below. Goldman is a manager or co-manager of a pending Oklo underwriting while cutting its Oklo PT to $49 from $57.

SMR licensing progress: NRC issued the first US construction permit for a BWRX-300 at TVA's Clinch River (Sep 30), Holtec filed its PSAR for two SMR-300s at Palisades, and Blue Energy filed its first construction permit application. Bechtel will step away as EPC contractor on TerraPower's Natrium project after the current phase.

AtkinsRéalis signed an MOU for up to eight CANDU reactors (6GW) in Indiana, valued by JPMorgan at ~$12-24B. CIBC calls it a modest positive but highly preliminary. The Nuclear Company floated a 6.6GW Kentucky campus that so far is a site.

Goldman: spot U3O8 was around $90/lb through September and into October, long-term price a record $96/lb, but September spot volumes were the lowest monthly level since December 2009. Sprott Physical Uranium Trust was absent in September, and 2026 term volumes are tracking below the five-year average. Spot conversion is down 3% on the month and 6% over three months, while SWU is up 287% over five years.
Yuanta flagged Solstice (SOLS) as the only US nuclear fuel conversion facility. Starboard disclosed a stake and called the stock stupid cheap.
Of ~80 reactors under construction globally, 38 are in China, 8 in India and 7 in Russia. All five 2026 grid connections on Goldman's list are Chinese.

Barclays counts policy reversals toward nuclear: Italy's Senate, Switzerland lifting its ban (referendum pending 2027), Belgium moving toward a state takeover of Engie's fleet, Taiwan clearing Maanshan restart plan (as soon as 2028). Goldman adds the Dutch scrapped Borssele's 2033 shutdown date. Barclays concludes policy risk is easing.
Hungary's government is considering replacing Rosatom as main contractor on Paks II, originally estimated at €12.5 billion with more than €2 billion already spent.

Samsung Securities expects the Nov 3 midterms to influence the pace rather than the direction of nuclear policy. Soft spots are executive-order items: $17.5 billion of conditional DOE loans for AP1000 components and the NRC overhaul. A Democratic House could hold hearings and subpoena.
HSBC raised its US data center demand forecast by 80% to ~900TWh in 2030. JPMorgan notes SpaceX's scenario of adding 20GW of incremental power next year, with high confidence in at least 10 GW.
The author's view: owners of licensed, grid-connected reactors (CEG, VST, TLN) are probably oversold, while pre-revenue developers likely face more dilution before bottoming.

tension_points.bull_case: Existing reactor owners have tax credit floor of c$45/MWh, PJM capacity payments, and hyperscaler PPAs, with Scotiabank estimating +~10% EPS from the Google deal.
tension_points.bear_case: PPA pricing is undisclosed, easy uprate megawatts are committed, and pre-revenue developers face dilution and financing risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: PTC is only guaranteed through 2032 and affordability pressure and regulation could slow contracting (HSBC).

theme_stances.key_argument: Existing licensed reactors are the cheapest and fastest nuclear megawatts, backed by tax credits and hyperscaler contracts.
theme_stances.evidence: the cheapest, fastest nuclear megawatt is the one that already exists

theme_stances.key_argument: Developers need more capital and face dilution before bottoming.
theme_stances.evidence: more dilution ahead before it bottoms
